syllabus_metadata.title: Chemistry Syllabus for Ordinary Secondary Education
syllabus_metadata.subject: Chemistry

competences.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
competences.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry

learning_activities.activity: (a) Describe the modern concept of atomic structure (Dalton's atomic structure and sub-atomic particles)
teaching_learning_methods: Think-ink-pair-share: Guide students in pair to think about the meaning of an atom and its structure
Technological-based learning: Guide students to account for the structure of an atom basing on ICT facilities and write a report
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The modern concept of atomic structure is clearly described
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Diagrams, pictures, wall charts, simulations and videos illustrating Dalton's atomic structure and sub-atomic particles

learning_activities.activity: (b) Describe the concept of electronic arrangements in atoms
teaching_learning_methods: Technological-based learning: Guide students to watch visual aids for simulations and animations, showing the arrangements of electrons in atoms of elements in their shells and write a report
Group activity: Assign students in manageable groups to practice the arrangement of electrons in shells of atoms of different elements through models designing using locally available materials
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of electronic arrangements in atoms is clearly described
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Diagrams, pictures, wall charts, simulations and videos illustrating energy shell diagram, and locally available materials for designing electronic models

learning_activities.activity: (c) Use the concept of atomic structure to determine the atomic and mass numbers of an element
teaching_learning_methods: Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to calculate the atomic number and mass number of an element for the given compound
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Atomic numbers and mass numbers of elements are correctly determined
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Models, charts and pictures showing the atomic number of elements, and wall charts showing the number of protons and neutrons of elements

learning_activities.activity: (d) Explain the concept of chemical formulae and nomenclature (valence, oxidation state, radicals and naming of binary inorganic compounds using the IUPAC system)
teaching_learning_methods: Inquiry-based learning: Assign students to collect commonly used substances and give their common names and identify their constituent elements
Group discussion: Guide student in manageable groups to describe the concepts of chemical formula, valence, oxidation state, radicals and name binary inorganic compounds using the IUPAC system
Gallery work: Guide students to brainstorm and share key rules in writing chemical formulae
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of chemical formulae and nomenclature are clearly explained
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Valence cards, modern periodic table, wall charts showing oxidation states and common radicals, and labelled bottles containing different laboratory chemicals

learning_activities.activity: (e) Determine empirical and molecular formulae of common compounds
teaching_learning_methods: Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to determine percentage compositions of each element and in a compound
Problem solving: Guide students to apply steps for calculating empirical formulae and molecular formulae of different compounds
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Empirical formulae and molecular formulae of different compounds are correctly determined
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Model depicting empirical formulae and molecular formulae, wall charts showing molecular formulae and modern periodic table

learning_activities.activity: (f) Describe the concept of chemical bonding (covalent and electrovalent bonding)
teaching_learning_methods: Outdoor activity: Guide students to reflect on real-environment about bonding such as building blocks erecting a walls and relate with the concepts of bonding
Technological-based learning: Use software such as ChemDraw to demonstrate the process of bonding
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of chemical bonding is clearly described
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Selected organic and inorganic structures, Computers installed with Chemistry software

learning_activities.activity: (g) Describe the concept of chemical reactions (chemical equations, balancing chemical equations, and types of chemical reactions)
teaching_learning_methods: Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to write simple word equations and chemical equations with symbols
Think-ink-pair-share: Guide students in pairs to identify types of chemical reactions, balance chemical equations, interpret word equations into chemical equations
Experimentation: Guide students to perform an experiment to verify the law of conservation of matter and write the report
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of chemical reactions is clearly described
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Kerosene, candles, KOH/NaOH, HCl, glycerine, selected apparatus and equipment

learning_activities.activity: (h) Relate the types of chemical reactions with common processes in daily life such as burning of fuel and digestion in living organisms
teaching_learning_methods: Project works: Task students to carry-out project to examine applications of chemical reactions in the burning of fuel and digestion in living organisms
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The types of chemical reactions are clearly related with common processes in daily life
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Laboratory note book, heat source and fuel such as charcoal

learning_activities.activity: (i) Describe acids, bases and salts (reactions of acids and bases with various substances) and their applications in daily life
teaching_learning_methods: Inquiry-based learning: Guide students to analyse various substances with acidic and basic properties commonly found in their environment and describe the concepts of acids, bases and salts
Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to describe the reactions of acids and bases
Field trips: Guide students to visit nearby food and beverages processing industries to examine the applications of acids, bases and salts
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The concepts of acids, bases and salts are clearly described
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Citrus fruits, vinegar, sour milk, apples, wood ash, tooth paste, baking powder, mineral acids, hydroxides and indicators

competences.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
competences.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of the physical and chemical properties of elements on the basis of their arrangements in the periodic table

learning_activities.activity: (a) Explain the changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements across and down the periodic table
teaching_learning_methods: Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to explain the trends of metallic and non-metallic elements across the periods and down the groups of the periodic table
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Changes in properties of elements across and down the periodic table are correctly explained
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Diagrams, pictures, wall charts, simulations and videos illustrating changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements across and down the periodic table

learning_activities.activity: (b) Use the electronic configuration of an element to locate their positions in the periodic table
teaching_learning_methods: Group discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to apply the periodic law in locating elements in the periodic table
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The electronic configurations of elements are correctly used to locate the positions of elements in the periodic table
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Wall charts of modern periodic table showing electronic configuration of some elements

learning_activities.activity: (a) Prepare acid-base indicators using locally available materials
teaching_learning_methods: Outdoor activity: Guide students to prepare acid-base indicators from locally available materials and write reports
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Acid-base indicators are correctly prepared using locally available materials
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Coloured flowers, coloured leaves, mortar and pestle, pieces of clothes, heat source, tripod stand, lemon juice, tomato juice, sour milk, vinegar, soft drinks and NaOH

learning_activities.activity: (b) Use the prepared indicators to test acidity and alkalinity of substances found in the locality
teaching_learning_methods: Experimentation: Guide students to perform experiments using locally made indicators to test acidity and alkalinity of substances found in the locality
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Acidity and alkalinity of substances found in the locality are tested using the prepared indicators
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Locally prepared indicator, POP indicator, MO indicator, lemon juice, tomato juice, sour milk, vinegar and soft drinks
